label: 26 October – 1 November
notes: Cook in number order: fish and prawns first while they're freshest.
Breakfast is the same every day, about 10 minutes.
Menu approved by you on Thursday with the toggles. Souvlaki swapped for shakshuka.
Nutrition is estimated per serving from ingredient weights.

breakfast.title: Spinach, feta & tomato scramble on GF seeded toast, with kiwi

ingredients.item: Tesco Free From seeded bread (certified GF)

steps.text: Toast 2 slices of GF bread. From frozen it needs 2 toaster cycles.
Heat 1 tsp oil in a non-stick pan on medium for 1 min. Add the halved tomatoes for 2 min, then the spinach for 1 min, until wilted.
Beat 4 eggs with ⅛ tsp salt and ⅛ tsp pepper. Turn the heat to low, pour in and stir slowly for 2–3 min, until just set but still glossy. Take it off the heat; it keeps cooking.
Pile onto the toast, crumble over 15g feta each, and have a kiwi on the side (halve it and scoop with a spoon).

breakfast.tip: Feta is salty, so the eggs only get ⅛ tsp for both of you. Freeze half the loaf on Sunday so it stays fresh all week.

dinners.title: Mediterranean cod, butter beans, cherry tomatoes & spinach

ingredients.item: olive oil (1 tsp cod, 2 tsp pan)
salt (⅛ quinoa, ⅛ cod, ¼ beans)

steps.text: Quinoa: rinse 60g quinoa in a sieve for 30 sec. Put it in a small pan with 150ml water and ⅛ tsp salt. Bring to the boil, then lid on, lowest heat, 12 min. Off the heat, keep the lid on for 5 min, then fluff with a fork.
Cod: pat the fillets dry with kitchen roll. Rub with 1 tsp oil, ½ tsp smoked paprika, the zest of ½ lemon, ⅛ tsp salt and ⅛ tsp pepper.
Air Fryer: cod at 200°C for 8–10 min (8 for thin fillets). Done when the thickest part is opaque all the way through and flakes with a fork.

Meanwhile, beans: heat 2 tsp oil in a frying pan on medium for 1 min. Add the sliced garlic and ⅛ tsp chilli flakes and cook for 1 min, until the garlic is just pale gold. Don't let it brown, it turns bitter.
Add the halved tomatoes and cook for 3 min, until they start to burst. Add the drained beans, 60ml water, ¼ tsp salt and ⅛ tsp pepper. Simmer for 3 min.
Stir in the spinach a handful at a time, 1–2 min, until just wilted. Off the heat, stir in 15ml lemon juice and most of the parsley (keep 2 tsp to finish).
Taste the beans. If flat, add ⅛ tsp salt and 1 tsp lemon juice. Too sharp? Stir in 1 tsp olive oil.
Serve: quinoa, then the beans, with the cod on top and the last of the parsley.

dinners.tip: Butter beans in water are unsalted, so they need the ¼ tsp. The cod only gets ⅛ tsp: it's delicate and the beans carry the seasoning.

dinners.title: Thai red prawn curry with green beans & basmati

ingredients.item: Thai red curry paste (Blue Dragon pot)

steps.text: Rice: rinse 100g rice in a sieve under the cold tap for 30 sec. Put it in a pan with 175ml water and ¼ tsp salt. Bring to the boil, then lid on, lowest heat, 10 min. Off the heat, lid on, 5 min. Don't lift the lid.
Prep: trim the beans and cut them into 3cm lengths. Slice the pepper into 1cm strips. Pat the prawns dry with kitchen roll.
Heat 1 tsp oil in a wok or large pan on medium for 1 min. Add 35g curry paste and fry for 1 min, stirring, until it smells fragrant.
Shake the coconut tin, then pour it all in with 1 tsp fish sauce and ½ tsp honey. Bring to a gentle bubble.
Add the beans and pepper. Simmer for 4 min, until the beans are just tender but still bright green.
Add the prawns and simmer gently for 3–4 min, until pink all through and curled into a C. Don't boil hard or they toughen.
Off the heat, stir in 15ml lime juice (½ lime) and most of the coriander.

Taste: the paste and fish sauce season the curry, so it gets no salt of its own. If flat, add ½ tsp fish sauce. Too hot? Add 1 tsp lime juice and ½ tsp honey. Serve over the rice with lime wedges and the last coriander.

dinners.tip: Curry paste strength varies: 35g is medium-hot. Fridge the rest of the pot (covered) and use it within 5 days, or freeze it.

dinners.title: Harissa chicken, crispy aubergine & quinoa with lemon yoghurt

ingredients.item: red onion, in 8 wedges (from the fridge)
olive oil (1 tsp chicken, 2 tsp veg)
salt (¼ quinoa, ¼ chicken, ¼ veg, ⅛ yoghurt)

steps.text: Chicken: mix 2 tbsp harissa, 1 tsp oil, 1 tsp lemon juice, ¼ tsp salt and ⅛ tsp pepper in a bowl. Add the thighs whole and turn to coat. (Even better marinated overnight in the fridge.)
Quinoa: rinse 80g quinoa for 30 sec. Put it in a small pan with 200ml water and ¼ tsp salt. Bring to the boil, then lid on, lowest heat, 12 min. Off the heat, lid on, 5 min, then fluff.
Veg: toss the aubergine cubes and onion wedges with 2 tsp oil, ½ tsp cumin and ¼ tsp salt.

Air Fryer: veg at 200°C for 10 min, shaking at 5 min. Then lay the chicken flat on top and cook 14 min more, turning the chicken at 7 min. Done at 75°C in the thickest part, or when the juices run clear. The aubergine should be soft inside and browned at the edges.
Lemon yoghurt: stir 100g yoghurt with the grated ½ garlic clove, 1 tsp lemon juice and ⅛ tsp salt.
Toss the quinoa with 2 tsp lemon juice and most of the parsley.
Rest the chicken on a board for 2 min, then slice it 1cm thick.
Taste a piece of aubergine. If flat, add ⅛ tsp salt over the veg. Too spicy? More yoghurt. Serve: quinoa, veg, chicken, a big spoon of yoghurt and the last of the parsley.

dinners.tip: Harissa brings some salt, so the chicken only gets ¼ tsp. The quinoa and aubergine need their own.

dinners.title: Smoky beef & black bean chilli with rice

ingredients.item: lean beef mince 5%, defrosted in the fridge

steps.text: Rice: rinse 100g rice for 30 sec. Pan with 175ml water and ¼ tsp salt. Bring to the boil, then lid on, lowest heat, 10 min. Off the heat, lid on, 5 min.
Heat 1 tsp oil in a large frying pan on high for 1 min. Add the mince and break it up with a spoon. Cook 5 min, stirring, until browned with no pink left.
Turn to medium. Add 1 tsp oil, the onion and the pepper. Cook 4 min, stirring now and then, until the onion is soft and see-through.
Stir in the garlic, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp smoked paprika, ½ tsp oregano, ¼ tsp chilli flakes and 1 tbsp tomato paste. Cook 1 min, stirring so it doesn't catch.

Add the tomatoes, black beans, 100ml water, ½ tsp salt and ¼ tsp pepper. Simmer with the lid half on for 15 min, stirring every 5 min. It's ready when it's thick and a spoon dragged through leaves a trail. If it gets dry, add 50ml water.
Taste: if flat, add ⅛ tsp salt and a squeeze of lime. If it's too sharp, stir in ½ tsp honey.
Serve: rice, chilli, 30g yoghurt each, the coriander and lime wedges.

dinners.tip: Tinned tomatoes need the ½ tsp salt: there's no salty sauce in this one. The day before, move the mince and beans from the freezer to the fridge.

dinners.title: Feta & chickpea shakshuka

steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a 26–28cm frying pan (one with a lid) on medium for 1 min. Add the onion and pepper and cook for 6 min, stirring now and then, until soft.
Stir in the garlic, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp smoked paprika and ¼ tsp chilli flakes. Cook 1 min.
Add the tomatoes, chickpeas, 100ml water, ¼ tsp salt and ⅛ tsp pepper. Simmer for 10 min, stirring now and then, until thick enough that a spoon leaves a trail.
Taste the sauce now, before the eggs go in: if flat, add ⅛ tsp salt; if too sharp, ½ tsp honey. The feta will add salt at the end, so keep it a little under-seasoned.
Make 6 wells with a spoon and crack an egg into each. Sprinkle ⅛ tsp salt and ⅛ tsp pepper over the eggs. Lid on, low–medium, 6–8 min, until the whites are set and the yolks still wobble.
Off the heat, scatter over the feta and herbs. Serve 3 eggs each, straight from the pan.

dinners.tip: Check the eggs at 6 min: whites should be opaque, not clear. For firmer yolks, give it 2 more min.

tips: Chicken: put 300g in the fridge for 3. Freeze the other 300g, labelled, for a future week.
Freeze half the GF loaf. Toast it from frozen.
Wrap the coriander and parsley in damp kitchen roll in a box. They're used in 1–5.
Optional: cook the quinoa for 3 at the same time. 140g quinoa, 350ml water, ⅜ tsp salt, same method. Fridge 3's share within 1 hour and reheat it until piping hot.
Optional: cook 4's rice too. 200g rice, 350ml water, ½ tsp salt. Fridge half within 1 hour; reheat once only, until piping hot.
Optional: marinate the chicken in the harissa mix overnight for more flavour.
Move 2 × 150g bags of mince and the ½ tin of black beans from the freezer to the fridge.
Curry paste: about 15g left. Fridge it covered for up to 5 days, or freeze.
Harissa: about 60g left in the jar, fridge. Good stirred into yoghurt as a dip.
Limes: 1 in 2, 1 in 4, 3 spare for drinks. Lemons: ½ in 1, ½ in 3, 2 spare.
Red onions, peppers and garlic come from what you already have: 3 onions, 3 peppers, about 7 cloves this week.
Yoghurt: 160g used, the rest is for dips or with the pears.
